title: One leaf in the pot
hookLine: Krishna eats one leaf from Draupadi's empty pot and ten thousand hungry sages feel full; why food goes to God first and comes back as prasad
carry: when god is fed, everyone is fed
tomorrow: The paste meant for a king
last: THE WATER — THE GANGA CAME DOWN TO PURIFY.

lines: A POT THAT FEEDS THEM DAILY.
cards: The Pandavas are living in exile in the forest, and they have one treasure: a pot from the Sun god that gives food every day, until Draupadi has eaten. Then it's empty till morning. Their cousin Duryodhana knows this.

So he sends them a guest: the sage Durvasa, well-known for his temper, with ten thousand disciples, timed to arrive just after Draupadi has finished her meal. Durvasa says: we'll bathe in the river, then we eat.
Draupadi looks at the empty pot. If she can't feed them, the curse will be terrible. So she closes her eyes and calls Krishna.

teach.b: Krishna appears, and the first thing he says is: I'm hungry. Give me something to eat. Draupadi almost cries: there's nothing, that's the whole problem.
Bring the pot, he says. Stuck to the rim is one tiny leaf of cooked greens. Krishna eats it, and says: may the one who is the soul of the whole world be satisfied.
Down at the river, ten thousand sages suddenly feel completely full. They're too embarrassed to come back, and they slip away. That's how the Mahabharata tells it.

Here's the teaching. Krishna's line names it: God is the soul in every being, so feeding God is never feeding just one. An old Hindu picture puts it simply: water the root of a tree, and every branch is fed.
That's naivedya, today's word: food offered to God before anyone eats. The cook often doesn't taste it while cooking, because the first taste isn't theirs.
A little goes before the image on a clean plate, sometimes with a tulsi leaf on top, and sits for a few moments.

teach.h: PRASAD: IT COMES BACK FOR EVERYONE.
teach.b: Then the plate comes back, and it isn't just food anymore. It's prasad, grace, and it's shared with everyone: the family, the guest at the door, the neighbor.
People take it in the right hand, often with a small bow, and try not to refuse it. Feed God first, and the food comes back for all. That's why the laddus wait.

how: Many Hindus place a small portion of food, often a sweet or fruit, before the image at the home shrine as naivedya, wait a few moments, and then receive it back as prasad, grace, sharing it with everyone in the house and any guests.

games.q: one leaf, ten thousand fed — tap the pairs.
p: food every day until Draupadi eats
the offering, come back for everyone

s: Krishna filled the pot with a feast for the sages
he ate one leaf stuck to the rim, and the sages at the river felt full.
offered food is thrown away after puja
it comes back as prasad and is shared with everyone, even guests.
in the story's teaching, food offered to God reaches every being
feed the root, and every branch is fed: the offering reaches everyone.

games.q: puja is done and the plate of laddus comes back from the shrine. what fits today's teaching?
o: keep them all in your room: they're blessed now.
share them as prasad with everyone in the house.
leave them on the shrine until they go stale.
games.why: once offered, the food is prasad, and it comes back for everyone: the family, the guest at the door, the neighbor.

practice: Set something small to eat in front of you, a piece of fruit, a square of chocolate, a few raisins, and pause before you eat it.

If you pray, offer it first, to Krishna or a name you honor, and wait a few breaths before you take it back as prasad. If you don't pray, hold it as a gift you didn't make by yourself: the sun, the farmer, the driver.
Then break it in two if you can, put half aside for someone else, and eat your half slowly.

wordCard.voice: Naivedya. Food offered to God before anyone eats, which comes back as prasad for everyone, like one leaf that fed ten thousand.

orig.note: Sanskrit naivedya: food offered to the deity. Once offered, it's received as prasad.

carryVoice: Your line: when God is fed, everyone is fed. One leaf from an empty pot. See you tomorrow.
